# Learnings and mistakes

No structural facts are generated for this page; the store has no concept of a mistake, only of records, decisions and handovers. Everything here is written by hand.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
MISTAKE, mine, cost four battery runs of about eleven minutes each: I
regenerated a generated document, then edited one of its sources, four separate
times. The booklet went stale twice, the book echoes once, and the quickstart's
verbatim copy of the workflow once. The order that works is every source edit
first, then replay_book.py --write, then regen_sandbox_guide.py, then sbe book,
then checksums LAST after git add. In this repository, changing a shipped file
means asking what quotes it.

MISTAKE, mine, and it wasted a full battery run: I waited on the battery with
`while pgrep -f "local-gates.sh"`, and the waiter's own command line contains
that string, so it matched itself and never exited. This is the pkill-by-pattern
lesson in the other direction. Wait on a sentinel file, not on a pattern.

MISTAKE, mine, twice: I read `EXIT=$?` after a pipeline ending in `tail`, so I
read tail's exit code and called a failing command green both times. Redirect to
a file and check the real exit code.

NEAR MISS, caught only by testing: I was about to relax a correct assertion. The
sandbox suite pins a commit hash and the guide's own prose says the hash varies,
so the assertion looked wrong. Running it twice showed the hash is deterministic,
and a generator exists for exactly this (tools/regen_sandbox_guide.py) under a
recorded founder decision to KEEP the pin. Relaxing it would have deleted the
property the test exists for.

LEARNING, the one worth carrying: fixing a check that was failing for one reason
exposed eighteen defects it had been masking. The artifacts check could not pass
its own worked example, so every hollow-tier scenario "passed" for the wrong
reason. A red check hides everything behind it.

LEARNING: under Actions, the client-name leak check SKIPPED on every run, because
it reads its list from a file in the operator's home directory and no hosted
runner has one. Local was better than Actions there and nobody knew.
<!-- bm-human:end -->
